extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors and newsroom staff reporting on LGBTQ+ people and issues
extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom stylebook providing terminology guidance and reporting standards for covering LGBTQ+ people, identities, health and policy with accuracy, sensitivity and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive, nonjudgmental language
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect inclusive coverage of LGBTQ+ people; use language that is sensitive and fair, without bias or judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guide complements publication prose stylebooks; it is updated regularly as language changes. Aim to avoid stigma, sensationalism and bias in all coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid terms that imply deception or ingenuine identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid phrases that assume someone’s sexual orientation or gender identity is deceptive, incongruous or ingenuine (e.g., 'straight-acting', 'He dressed as a girl', 'passes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Do not use 'straight-acting', 'passes', or 'dressed as' — these can be unfounded, insensitive or defamatory. Use only in direct quotes or when clearly accurate and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false balance in coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not give discredited or opposing views unnecessary weight when it is insensitive or would perpetuate falsehoods (false balance / bothsidesism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious citing scientifically or ethically discredited views (e.g., anti-LGBTQ 'experts'); include opposing views only if they genuinely further understanding. Consider neutral views as alternatives and contextualize sources’ authority or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid politically charged shorthand labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using politically charged terms that politicize or disparage LGBTQ+ people (e.g., 'bathroom bill', 'gay agenda', 'special rights', 'gender ideology').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more specific, neutral phrasing; reserve charged terms for direct quotations and fact-check when they are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gender-neutral language for events and industry terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer gender-neutral terms for industry events and products (e.g., 'wedding expo' instead of 'bridal expo').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessarily gendered words like 'bridal' when broader or gender-neutral language is accurate and clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bride/groom usage — ask subject preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Bride/groom acceptable for female/male members of a couple, but verify and ask subjects which term they prefer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain, use gender-neutral terms like 'partner' or 'person'; be mindful such gendered terms may not apply to all individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ally — definition and caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'ally' as a person who supports LGBTQ+ people and causes but does not personally identify as LGBTQ+; note some organizations object to including 'ally' in acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of variations in usage and objections to inclusion in acronyms such as LGBTQIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'biological' when referring to gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid terms like 'biological sex' or 'biological male/female' in reference to gender, because they are used politically to misconstrue gender identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If quotations include such terms, follow up with a fact check and prefer precise distinctions (sex assigned at birth vs gender identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Family and parent identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not differentiate families led by LGBTQ+ parents or identify parents' sexual orientation/gender identity unless relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid terms like 'gay families'; use 'families' or 'parents' and ask subjects how they wish to be identified. Do not mention conception techniques or genetic relationships unless relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gender-neutral partner/spouse language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'partner' or 'spouse' as acceptable gender-neutral terms; 'fiancé/fiancée' acceptable but ask subjects for preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For engaged people, gender-neutral options (engaged partner/person) are acceptable; ask individuals which terms they prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outing and 'out' terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid outing someone without consent or clear public relevance; use 'out' instead of 'openly' when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid words like 'acknowledged', 'avowed', 'admitted', 'confessed' because of inaccuracy or negative connotations. Use 'out' and be mindful of context and consequences of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'lifestyle' framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid describing LGBTQ+ identity as a 'lifestyle', which inaccurately implies choice or trivializes identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sexual orientation may be part of a person's life but is not a lifestyle; choose neutral, descriptive phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of slurs and slang
rubrics_metrics.description: Slang and slurs are acceptable only very rarely — usually only in quotations or when self-referential and there is a compelling reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider hyphenating slurs (e.g., f—) or follow organizational profanity policies. Examples given (dyke, fag, tranny) should be avoided except in narrow contexts and usually only in quotation with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misleading associations and defamatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid misleading associations that politicize, disparage or trivialize LGBTQ+ lives (terms like 'mutilation', 'grooming', 'pedophilia', 'sodomy' when used to stigmatize).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paraphrase or fact-check quotations containing such terms; avoid implying criminality or predation broadly about LGBTQ+ people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization names and false authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not treat groups opposing LGBTQ+ rights as authoritative without context; avoid false balance in sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such groups must be quoted or mentioned, describe their mission or actions in unbiased language and provide context on their credibility or aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'opposite sex' phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'opposite sex' which assumes a binary; use 'another sex' or 'different sex' instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise and inclusive in language about sex and gender where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage phrasing — do not modify 'marriage' unnecessarily
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid modifying 'marriage' (e.g., 'same-sex marriage') when unnecessary; there is no legal distinction in U.S. law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, prefer 'marriage for same-sex couples' or 'same-gender' phrasing; avoid colloquial modifiers like 'gay marriage' unless needed and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'pregnant people' when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'pregnant people' to include those who are or may become pregnant but who do not identify as women; avoid overly clinical alternatives when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider audience and specificity; avoid 'people with uteruses' as unnecessarily clinical in many contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spouse/gendered partner terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'spouse' as a gender-neutral term acceptable in all references; 'husband' or 'wife' fine if the subject uses them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask couples which terms they prefer before using gendered language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'gay' and 'lesbian' terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'gay' for men attracted to men, 'lesbian' for women attracted to women; do not use 'is a gay' as a noun construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask subjects for their preferred labels; 'gay' may be acceptable for women in some cases. Use precise phrasing and avoid outdated 'homosexual' for people.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBTQ+ umbrella phrasing and acronym use
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable to use 'LGBTQ+' in all references; be cautious about using 'the LGBTQ+ community' as it implies homogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose level of specificity (LGBTQ, LGBTQIA, LGBTQIA2S+) appropriate to audience and coverage; be aware acronyms can reflect generational, cultural or political distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: sexual orientation vs sexual identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual orientation refers to attraction (sexual, emotional, romantic); sexual identity is a person's perception of their own sexuality and may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imprecise terms like 'sexual preference' which implies choice; never assume orientation — ask when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume sexual orientation or gender identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Never infer a person's sexual orientation or gender identity from appearance, relationship history or community involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, ask respectfully how a source identifies and make sure they understand how it will be represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health reporting — avoid pathologizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use respectful, person-first language in health reporting; avoid stigmatizing terms and moral framing (e.g., 'victim', 'suffers from', 'afflicted with').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral terms like 'person with HIV' and describe symptoms, severity and prognosis factually without emotional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health reporting — contextualize disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextualize health disparities as often resulting from systemic bias, inequities, barriers to care and social determinants — not from sexual orientation/gender identity itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how structural factors (racism, poverty, policy barriers) contribute to disparities rather than implying causality from identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health reporting — avoid false causality
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not imply sexual orientation or gender identity causes poor health outcomes; explain contributing systemic factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence-based context and avoid simplistic cause-effect statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health reporting — seek underrepresented voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Include perspectives from trans people, LGBTQ+ people of color and those in rural areas to add depth and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach interviews with empathy and acknowledge fear of stigma may discourage participation; compensate by seeking multiple, credible sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health reporting — rely on culturally competent research
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult LGBTQ+ health experts and community organizations alongside mainstream sources (CDC, NIH, HHS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current, culturally competent research and identify when official sources may be disputed or politically influenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIV/AIDS terminology and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'HIV' for the virus and 'AIDS' for the syndrome; 'AIDS' acceptable in collective references and the S is uppercase; avoid 'full-blown AIDS'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use person-first phrasing ('person with AIDS'); explain difference between HIV and AIDS and that HIV-positive people may not have AIDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIV-positive / HIV-negative hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the hyphen in 'HIV-positive' and 'HIV-negative' in all instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant terms like 'HIV virus.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Undetectable = Untransmittable (U=U) — explain, avoid shorthand
rubrics_metrics.description: For people with an undetectable viral load due to ART, transmission risk is near zero; avoid using 'U=U' shorthand without explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly explain what undetectable viral load means rather than relying on the campaign shorthand.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrEP/PEP and related terms — correct phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'PrEP' for pre-exposure prophylaxis and 'PEP' for post-exposure prophylaxis; PrEP refers to the regimen, not the medication (e.g., 'He is on PrEP').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct grammar: 'He is on PrEP,' not 'He took his PrEP with breakfast.' Define doxyPEP/doxyPrEP when relevant and note differing evidence bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blood donation reporting — include policy context
rubrics_metrics.description: When relevant, report FDA and other blood donor requirements that may differentially affect men who have sex with men and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details about deferral or guidance (e.g., PrEP-related guidance) and avoid omitting facts that disproportionately affect queer communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suicide coverage guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach suicide coverage with care; use 'died by suicide' or 'killed themself' instead of 'committed suicide' and avoid dramatizing method/location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover suicide only with clear news value; avoid attributing single causes; frame as a preventable public health concern and include crisis resources early in the story (e.g., 988).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of historical/clinical terms for intersex
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'intersex' for people born with variations of sex characteristics; avoid 'hermaphrodite' and 'disorders of sex development' unless clinically necessary and with explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to specific conditions (e.g., Turner syndrome) when relevant and explain them; do not conflate intersex with transgender or nonbinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadname/birth name and obituaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid deadnaming (using a trans person’s birth name they no longer use) unless you have express permission; in obituaries, use the name and gender identity the person used in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about outing in obituaries; list partners equivalently and avoid revealing deadnames without consent or clear relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronouns practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the pronouns a source uses for themself; confirm when uncertain and prioritize clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the phrase 'preferred pronouns' and 'chosen pronouns'; accept singular they without needing explanation. For multiple pronouns, find ways to include all without confusing the reader; consider delaying publication if clarification is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transgender identification and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify people as transgender only when relevant and if they are widely known or describe themselves as such; otherwise refer to someone by their gender (e.g., 'man', 'woman').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'transgendered'; avoid disclosing gender history or trans status without informed consent; exercise special care with reporting on children and in contexts of political hostility to gender-affirming care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology to avoid for transgender people
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use 'transgendered', 'transgenderism', 'sex change', 'pre-op'/'post-op', or 'transsexual' (unless preferred by the subject).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'transgender', 'trans', 'gender-affirming care', 'gender-affirmation surgery' and avoid medicalizing or sensational terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-affirming care reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to treatments (counseling, puberty blockers, hormones, surgery) as 'gender-affirming care' and avoid calling them 'mutilation' or other dehumanizing language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overemphasize surgery in transitions; avoid obsolete abbreviations (GAS/GCS/SRS); explain dispute or politicization and note that major medical groups support such care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detransition reporting cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assume motives for detransition; do not use politicized labels like 'detransitioner' without context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that anecdotes about detransition are often used by opponents of gender-affirming care and that evidence suggests regret is rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender categories and inclusive phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between sex assigned at birth, gender identity and gender expression as needed for clarity; use inclusive wording such as 'people of all genders' when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise about which concept you are addressing; e.g., use 'same-sex/different-sex' vs 'same-gender/different-gender' appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonbinary / genderqueer / agender usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'nonbinary', 'genderqueer', 'agender' when people self-identify as such; these terms are distinct from sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only when relevant and when subjects describe themselves that way; explain unfamiliar terms without pathologizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-spirit usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'two-spirit' only in broad references or if an individual uses it; lowercase and hyphenate unless part of a proper name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the adjective 'two-spirited'; explain tribal and individual variation when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drag and cross-dressing distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'drag performer' as a gender-neutral term; clarify that drag is a performance art not synonymous with transgender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'drag queen' or 'drag king' where appropriate; for events like 'Drag Story Hour' use correct capitalization when referring to the nonprofit network and 'drag story hour' for generic references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reclaimed or reclaimed-pejorative terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Words once pejorative (e.g., 'dyke', 'queer', 'queen') may be reclaimed by some members; use with caution and generally only when subjects use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If including such terms, consider audience and include context; do not use them as epithets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion therapy / 'ex-gay' reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to 'conversion therapy' in quotation marks and always include context that it is discredited and often banned for minors; treat 'ex-gay' similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate opposition by major medical/mental health groups and legal restrictions when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSM and behavioral categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'MSM' (men who have sex with men) as a behavioral and public-health category that does not imply identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify that MSM is not synonymous with gay or bisexual men and use in appropriate medical or scientific contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology for sexual- and romantic-orientation variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and use terms like 'asexual', 'aromantic', 'demisexual', 'graysexual', 'pansexual' accurately and distinguish them from gender terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain prefixes (demi-, gray-) and meanings when relevant; avoid conflating sexual orientation with gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on policy and legislation — precision and context
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering legislation/policy affecting LGBTQ+ people, provide factual context about impacts and avoid framing rights as controversial opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about what a law does (e.g., access to restrooms, restrictions on gender-affirming care); include voices of affected people and experts and avoid sensational framing.
